description: Execute a datacenter exit for a legacy on-premises application, migrating it to a public cloud (AWS). The app runs on 4 physical Windows servers behind a hardware load balancer, with a SQL Server backend and a file share. The migration must follow this sequence: provision cloud infrastructure (EC2, RDS, EFS), replicate data (database backup/restore + file sync), establish network connectivity (VPN/DirectConnect), run a dual-run period (traffic to both on-prem and cloud), execute cutover (DNS flip + load balancer drain), verify in cloud, and decommission the on-prem datacenter (shut down servers, cancel rack lease, dispose of hardware). A rollback plan must exist for the cutover step (DNS revert, re-enable on-prem load balancer). Risk factors: data sync gaps during dual-run, DNS TTL caching delaying cutover, hardware decommission is irreversible (cannot re-provision physical servers quickly), and SQL Server licensing differences. Tools available: AWS Migration Hub, DMS (Database Migration Service), DataSync, Route 53, PowerShell, SSMS.
